usa-fed-cut-2024.title: The Fed cuts rates by 50 basis points
usa-fed-cut-2024.summary: The first cut since 2020: the Fed chooses a bold move to keep the labor market from deteriorating too fast, as inflation approaches 2%.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: The Federal Reserve lowers its target range from 5.25-5.50% to 4.75-5.00%. That is a 50 bp cut, larger than the customary 25 bp.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: The cost of credit falls for households and firms. Housing, investment, and refinancing get cheaper, which supports demand.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: Long rates fall, the dollar weakens, and US equities rise. Growth-stock valuations benefit from the lower discount rate.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: borrowers, equities, dollar-indebted emerging markets. Losers: cash savers, banks whose margins compress, dollar traders.

history.title: The Fed eases, yet the recession comes
history.text: In 2001, the Fed cut rates aggressively in the face of the slowdown. It did not keep equities from falling: the market always anticipates the economy before the central bank does.

concepts.definition: The reference rate set by the central bank, which influences the cost of credit across the whole economy.
The rate used to bring future cash flows back to today's value. The lower it is, the dearer long-dated assets become.
Rate cuts or asset purchases intended to support activity.

china-stimulus-2024.title: Beijing unveils a stimulus package
china-stimulus-2024.summary: Rate cuts, credit support, and property measures: China tries to revive domestic demand weakened by the developers' crisis.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: The PBoC cuts several policy rates and eases credit conditions. Measures support the property market and equities.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Builders and local governments breathe, but households stay cautious. Credit transmission is slowed by deleveraging.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: The Shanghai Composite logs its best rebound in a decade. The yuan stays constrained and foreign investors return cautiously.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: developers, banks, Chinese cyclicals, commodities. Losers: savers, short sellers, commodity importers.

history.title: The stimulus plan that changed everything
history.text: Facing the global crisis, Beijing had launched a massive infrastructure program. Growth came back quickly, but local debt and the property bubble were the side effects.

concepts.definition: The effect of public spending on activity: one euro spent can generate more than one euro of GDP.
Reducing debt among households, firms, or the state, often at the cost of weaker demand.
A broad, persistent fall in prices that makes agents postpone purchases and raises the burden of debt.

france-spread-2024.title: The France-Germany spread widens after the dissolution
france-spread-2024.summary: The announcement of snap legislative elections sends the French risk premium up. Investors demand a higher yield to lend to Paris.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: The president dissolves the National Assembly after the European elections. No clear majority emerges, making the budget and reforms uncertain.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Firms postpone investment decisions. The deficit path becomes less credible while debt already exceeds 110% of GDP.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: The French OAT yield rises and the spread against the German Bund widens. French banks and domestic names underperform.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: German Bunds, opportunistic bond investors. Losers: French taxpayers, banks, firms dependent on the home market.

history.title: When the euro area nearly broke apart
history.text: The sovereign debt crisis showed that a euro-area country can lose market confidence without controlling its currency. The 'spread' had become the euro's survival thermometer.

concepts.definition: The yield gap between two bonds of the same maturity. It measures the risk premium the market demands.
The French government bond, named in the market after its French acronym.
The extra yield demanded when political uncertainty threatens the fiscal path.

japan-boj-2024.title: The BOJ normalizes and the carry trade unravel
japan-boj-2024.summary: Japan exits negative rates, then raises its rate. The yen strengthens abruptly and triggers a global unwinding of the carry trade.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: The Bank of Japan ends eight years of negative rates in March, then raises its rate in July. It also reduces its bond purchases.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Credit becomes marginally more expensive, but the yen appreciates. Exporters lose competitiveness while households pay less for imports.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: Investors who borrowed in yen to buy high-yield assets must unwind positions. Global equity markets tumble in early August.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: Japanese banks, the yen, importers. Losers: exporters, carry-trade hedge funds, overvalued risky assets.

history.title: The bubble's comeuppance
history.text: Japan had already suffered a major monetary shock when the BOJ tightened to break the bubble. Equities and real estate took decades to recover.

concepts.definition: Borrowing in a low-rate currency to invest in a higher-yielding asset. Highly profitable as long as the funding currency stays weak.
A policy rate below zero: banks pay to deposit their cash at the central bank.
A central bank's gradual return to more conventional rates and balance sheets.

saudi-oil-cuts-2024.title: Riyadh extends its oil-production cuts
saudi-oil-cuts-2024.summary: To support the barrel price, Saudi Arabia keeps output reduced. It protects per-unit revenue but sacrifices volume and growth.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: Riyadh and its allies extend voluntary production cuts. The aim is to avoid an oversupply that would send prices falling.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Oil revenues fall in volume, GDP contracts, and the budget deficit widens. Vision 2030 projects must be funded by debt or the PIF.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: Oil prices stabilize, but the stock market and Saudi banks depend on public spending. CDS stay low thanks to reserves.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: high-cost producers, oil importers. Losers: oil economies, energy-services firms, fuel consumers.

history.title: The price war that drained the reserves
history.text: Saudi Arabia had raised output to defend market share. The barrel collapsed below 30 dollars, forcing the kingdom to draw on reserves and launch Vision 2030.

concepts.definition: An enlarged producers' cartel that coordinates quotas to influence the oil price.
Revenue from the gap between extraction cost and selling price. It funds the state without going through taxes.
The barrel price needed to balance the budget. The higher it is, the more vulnerable the country is to falling prices.

uae-corporate-tax-2023.title: The Emirates introduce a corporate tax
uae-corporate-tax-2023.summary: A country with near-zero taxation adopts a 9% levy on profits. A turning point for a model that drew corporate headquarters with the absence of tax.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: The Emirates introduce a 9% federal corporate tax above a profit threshold, with exemptions for qualifying free zones.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Firms must rework their structures and transfer prices. Low-margin activities become less attractive while high-value services stay competitive.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: Revenues diversify beyond oil. Investors watch compliance and the real substance of structures.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: the federal budget, consulting firms, high-margin activities. Losers: shell companies, low-margin traders, rival offshore jurisdictions.

history.title: VAT changes the social contract
history.text: The Emirates had introduced a 5% VAT as oil rent no longer sufficed. The corporate tax extends this transition to modern taxation.

concepts.definition: Prices applied between subsidiaries of the same group. They determine where profits are taxed.
A separate customs and fiscal territory designed to attract exporting firms.
The gradual replacement of oil revenues by taxes and levies on the real economy.

morocco-worldcup-2030.title: Morocco will co-host the 2030 World Cup
morocco-worldcup-2030.summary: With Spain and Portugal, Morocco wins the co-hosting of the 2030 tournament. The country accelerates investment in stadiums, transport, and hotels.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: The Ibero-Moroccan bid is selected. Morocco becomes the first African country to co-host a World Cup, after the 2025 Africa Cup.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Infrastructure, stadium, and hotel construction supports growth and jobs. The risk is over-scaled investment after the event.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: Construction, cement, tourism, and bank stocks rise. The state borrows more but gains an image effect.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: construction, tourism, banks, real estate. Losers: taxpayers if costs overrun, sectors neglected by the building priority.

history.title: South Africa and the World Cup effect
history.text: South Africa's tournament left costly, little-used stadiums. It also improved the country's image. The lesson: infrastructure must serve after the event, not only during it.

concepts.definition: The market's reaction before the spending or revenue even materializes.
The impact of public investment on activity, strongest when the economy has idle capacity.
What you give up by assigning a resource to one use rather than another.

south-africa-gnu-2024.title: The ANC forms a government of national unity
south-africa-gnu-2024.summary: For the first time since 1994, the ANC loses its majority. A coalition with the opposition opens a new political era and hope for reforms.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: The ANC takes about 40% of the vote. It allies with the DA and other parties to form a government of national unity.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: The coalition can speed up power and logistics reforms, but it may also be paralyzed by internal disagreements.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: The rand and bonds firm up on hopes of better governance. CDS fall, yet remain elevated.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: banks, retailers, local bonds. Losers: firms reliant on public patronage, populist parties.

history.title: The transition that avoided war
history.text: The end of apartheid was negotiated, not torn away by revolution. The compromise stabilized the country but left most inherited economic structures intact.

concepts.definition: An executive formed by several parties that must share power and negotiate every reform.
The extra yield demanded when the stability of public decision-making is uncertain.
A measure that changes how the economy works: labor market, energy, competition, taxation.

lebanon-ceasefire-2024.title: A ceasefire ends the hostilities with Israel
lebanon-ceasefire-2024.summary: After months of war, a ceasefire is agreed. It opens a window for reconstruction but resolves neither the banking collapse nor the political crisis.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: Israel and Hezbollah accept a halt to hostilities, with a deployment of the Lebanese army and an international monitoring mechanism.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Displacement slows and humanitarian aid can move. Reconstruction will cost billions, in a state without budget capacity.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: Lebanese markets stay illiquid. The pound and deposits do not recover their value; no CDS allows pricing the risk.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: displaced people, reconstruction, importers. Losers: insolvent banks, sovereign creditors, savers frozen out.

history.title: The 33-day war
history.text: The 2006 conflict had already destroyed infrastructure and displaced nearly a million people. Reconstruction was donor-funded, without fixing the political fragilities.

concepts.definition: The risk that a conflict, a sanction, or a military decision abruptly changes asset values.
A situation in which a state does not repay its debt on the terms agreed.
The use of a foreign currency for transactions and savings, a sign of lost confidence in the local currency.

syria-assad-fall-2024.title: The fall of the Assad regime opens an uncertain transition
syria-assad-fall-2024.summary: A lightning rebel offensive ends fifty years of family rule. Syria begins a political and economic reconstruction without solid institutions.

chain.label: Event
chain.text: Rebel forces enter Damascus. Bashar al-Assad leaves the country. Security and power structures collapse within days.

chain.label: Economic consequence
chain.text: Some sanctions could be lifted, but the economy is destroyed, the currency nearly worthless, and the skills gone. Emergency aid dominates.

chain.label: Financial consequence
chain.text: There is no rating, no CDS, and no liquid equity market. The risk cannot be priced: it is treated as maximal.

chain.label: Winners / losers
chain.text: Winners: the freed population, reconstruction, trading neighbors. Losers: the old regime's networks, undocumented creditors, threatened minorities.

history.title: The Arab Spring and the war
history.text: The 2011 protests demanded freedoms and jobs. Repression turned dissent into civil war, with an internationalization that destroyed the country.

concepts.definition: Uncertainty linked to the absence of reliable data, which prevents valuing an asset correctly.
Restrictive measures that limit access to trade, financing, and technology.
Reinvestment in infrastructure and institutions after a conflict. It can support growth but also breeds corruption risks.
